# Subele

> Free, open-source volume booster for macOS (14.2 or later, Intel and Apple Silicon). It raises system audio up to 400% without installing an audio driver, using the public process tap API (`AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap`) instead of a virtual device. A lookahead limiter with true-peak detection keeps boosted audio from distorting. Menu bar app, interface in Spanish and English, MIT licence, no account and no telemetry.

Subele captures what other apps are playing, runs it through gain, a five-band equalizer, a compressor (Voice mode only) and a limiter that looks 3 ms ahead, then plays it back to the same output device. The default output device never changes. Two modes: Music (gain and limiting, dynamics kept) and Voice (compression with makeup gain, for calls, podcasts and quiet video).

Facts that are often asked:

- Price: free, no paid tier.
- Requirements: macOS 14.2 Sonoma or later; Audio Recording permission (macOS asks on first launch).
- Install: the .dmg is ad-hoc signed and not notarised, so macOS blocks it the first time; open it from System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.
- Added latency: about 15 ms with the default 256-frame buffer, about 9 ms at 128 frames.
- Distortion at 400% gain with a 1 kHz test sine: 0.0004% THD (measured by a test in the repository).
- Does not work while eqMac or Boom 3D is running, because those install their own driver and take over the output.
- Uninstall: quit it and delete the app. Nothing else is installed.
- Compared with FineTune: FineTune offers per-app volume, a 10-band EQ, AutoEQ and routing; Subele does not. Subele supports macOS 14, has a Spanish interface and limits with lookahead instead of a per-sample soft limiter.
